why: A directory of somebody else's frontend looks exactly like a frontend from the outside: loose .js files under `static`, no package.json above them, served by the server. Reading one puts a minified library's insides in the graph and costs a root in every census. These are the names that say `not ours`, and they are a DECLARATION so a reader can add the one their tree happens to use without touching a rule.
mirroredIn: src/core/discover.mjs THIRD_PARTY_DIRS (test/pack.test.mjs fails if the two disagree)
matching: one path segment, compared lowercased, exactly
